### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. oculopharyngeal muscular dystrophy 2  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.729)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:5033)

**Proposed mechanism:** HNRNPA2B1 (HGNC:5033) —DISRUPTS→ RNA processing and transport (GO:0006396); RNA processing and transport (GO:0006396) —LEADS_TO→ Ptosis (HP:0000508); RNA processing and transport (GO:0006396) —LEADS_TO→ Muscle weakness (HP:0001324). Haploinsufficiency of HNRNPA2B1 disrupts normal RNA processing and transport, leading to both ptosis and muscle weakness, which are key phenotypes in both MONDO:0014178 and oculopharyngeal muscular dystrophy 2.

**How to falsify it:** The presence of loss-of-function variants in HNRNPA2B1 with a minor allele frequency > 1% in gnomAD would falsify the haploinsufficiency model for both diseases. _(variant: HGMD:CDLM227417)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of HNRNPA2B1 in RNA processing and transport may lead to therapeutic strategies that target this pathway for both MONDO:0014178 and oculopharyngeal muscular dystrophy 2.

---

#### 2. Finnish upper limb-onset distal myopathy  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.498)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-72163, Reactome:R-HSA-72203, Reactome:R-HSA-9770562, Reactome:R-HSA-9918481)

**Proposed mechanism:** HNRNPA1 (HGNC:4842) —DISRUPTS→ RNA binding and processing (GO:0000952); HNRNPA2B1 (HGNC:4841) —DISRUPTS→ RNA binding and processing (GO:0000952); RNA binding and processing (GO:0000952) —LEADS_TO→ Cytoplasmic mRNA processing (GO:0000950); Cytoplasmic mRNA processing (GO:0000950) —LEADS_TO→ Muscle weakness (HP:0001324); Cytoplasmic mRNA processing (GO:0000950) —LEADS_TO→ Distal muscle weakness (HP:0002460). Mutations in HNRNPA1 and HNRNPA2B1 disrupt normal RNA binding and processing, leading to aberrant cytoplasmic mRNA processing. This disruption ultimately contributes to muscle weakness phenotypes observed in both MONDO:0014178 and Finnish upper limb-onset distal myopathy.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in HNRNPA1 or HNRNPA2B1 with a clear loss-of-function mechanism, or conversely, a complete lack of overlap in the specific RNA processing pathways affected by mutations in these genes in the two diseases. _(variant: rs113355123)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared molecular mechanisms involving HNRNPA1 and HNRNPA2B1 in these distinct but mechanistically linked myopathies could reveal common therapeutic targets for modulating RNA processing or mitigating the downstream effects of aberrant protein aggregation or function.

#### 3. inclusion body myopathy with early-onset Paget disease with or without frontotemporal dementia 3  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.485)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-72163, Reactome:R-HSA-72203, Reactome:R-HSA-9770562, Reactome:R-HSA-9918481)

**Proposed mechanism:** HNRNPA1 (HGNC:4877) —DISRUPTS→ RNA binding and processing (GO:0003723); HNRNPA2B1 (HGNC:4878) —DISRUPTS→ RNA binding and processing (GO:0003723); RNA binding and processing (GO:0003723) —LEADS_TO→ Protein aggregation (GO:0000428); HNRNPA1 (HGNC:4877) —LEADS_TO→ Protein aggregation (GO:0000428); HNRNPA2B1 (HGNC:4878) —LEADS_TO→ Protein aggregation (GO:0000428); Protein aggregation (GO:0000428) —LEADS_TO→ Paget disease of bone (HP:0002651); Protein aggregation (GO:0000428) —LEADS_TO→ Frontotemporal dementia (HP:0001299); Protein aggregation (GO:0000428) —LEADS_TO→ Myopathy (HP:0003201). Mutations in HNRNPA1 and HNRNPA2B1 disrupt normal RNA binding and processing, leading to the aggregation of misfolded proteins. This protein aggregation is a shared mechanism that ultimately results in the distinct yet overlapping phenotypes of myopathy, Paget disease of bone, and frontotemporal dementia.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that the mutations in HNRNPA1 and HNRNPA2B1 associated with disease A do not lead to protein aggregation or affect RNA binding and processing, or that these processes are not implicated in disease B. _(variant: Presence of the specific disease-causing variants in HNRNPA1 or HNRNPA2B1 at a high frequency (>1%) in the gnomAD database.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism of RNA binding dysfunction and protein aggregation mediated by HNRNPA1 and HNRNPA2B1 could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting protein homeostasis or RNA processing that benefit patients with both inclusion body myopathy and frontotemporal dementia associated with these genes, as well as Paget disease of bone.

#### 4. amyotrophic lateral sclerosis type 20  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.484)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-72163, Reactome:R-HSA-72203, Reactome:R-HSA-9770562, Reactome:R-HSA-9918481)

**Proposed mechanism:** HNRNPA1 (HGNC:4847) —DISRUPTS→ RNA binding and processing (GO:0000952); HNRNPA2B1 (HGNC:4848) —DISRUPTS→ RNA binding and processing (GO:0000952); HNRNPA1 (HGNC:4847) —LEADS_TO→ Cytoplasmic mislocalization of RNA-binding proteins (null); HNRNPA2B1 (HGNC:4848) —LEADS_TO→ Cytoplasmic mislocalization of RNA-binding proteins (null); Cytoplasmic mislocalization of RNA-binding proteins (null) —LEADS_TO→ Motor neuron degeneration (HP:0007239); Cytoplasmic mislocalization of RNA-binding proteins (null) —LEADS_TO→ Frontotemporal dementia (HP:0000875). Mutations in HNRNPA1 and HNRNPA2B1 disrupt normal RNA binding and processing, leading to cytoplasmic mislocalization of these proteins. This mislocalization is hypothesized to cause both motor neuron degeneration (ALS20) and frontotemporal dementia (FTD-ALS).

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in HNRNPA1 and HNRNPA2B1 cause distinct, non-overlapping molecular pathways leading to motor neuron degeneration and frontotemporal dementia, respectively, without any shared intermediate molecular defects. _(variant: Identification of common variants (AF > 1%) in gnomAD within the critical functional domains of HNRNPA1 or HNRNPA2B1 that do not segregate with either disease.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism of RNA processing defects and protein mislocalization in these related neurodegenerative diseases could lead to the development of targeted therapies aimed at restoring normal RNA metabolism or protein localization, potentially benefiting patients with both conditions.
